Genetic testing confirming a pathogenic TSC1 mutation and brain MRI revealing subcortical tubers provide definitive molecular and imaging evidence, fulfilling diagnostic criteria. Benign idiopathic infantile seizures and acquired symptomatic epilepsy are refuted by the confirmed genetic mutation, subcortical tubers, normal psychomotor development, and absence of focal neurological deficits or acquired structural causes. Therefore, the consensus diagnosis is tuberous sclerosis complex, with high confidence.
